_readme: THE MAIN PAGE CONTROL PANEL. Edit a value, save, and the main page follows.

Clearing a value, or removing its line, REMOVES what it feeds rather than leaving a hole — empty the event and the event card goes; empty its end time and the card stays but loses its countdown. A value the page cannot read costs only the thing it feeds, never the page.
featured  — the article in the big featured card. Its picture comes from the article itself, so the page name is all there is to set.

event     — the event card. starts/ends drive its countdown, written YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in UTC. Leave starts empty for something already under way. See PICKING AN EVENT PICTURE below for banner and image.

patches   — the build chips at the top of the page, one per entry. channel LIVE gets the filled marker and its entry also fills the 'this patch' card; anything else gets the hollow one. Add a chip by adding an entry.
hero      — the big picture, the two-tone headline over it, and the phrases that cycle through the search box.
chips     — the row of links under the hero.
directory — the groups of links at the very bottom of the page.
A link is { page, label } for somewhere on this wiki, or { url, label } for somewhere else. label is optional on a wiki link.
Putting a _ in front of a key PARKS it: the page stops reading it but the value stays here for when you want it back. That is how the unused event picture below is kept.
PICKING AN EVENT PICTURE — the event card has two designs and the picture you set chooses between them, so set one key or the other, not both. Setting both uses banner.

banner  — one of the strips from Category:Main page banner images. It runs across the top of the card at the height it was drawn, and the card shows the MIDDLE of it: about two thirds on a wide screen, about a quarter on a phone. Check that the logo is somewhere near the middle of the file rather than out at an edge, or a narrow screen loses it.

image   — an ordinary screenshot. It stands in a column beside the text on a wide screen and across the top on a narrow one, so its subject wants to be near the middle. A banner strip set here comes out a smear; use banner for those.
